Link does not have a discernible accessible name

Why this matters

Screen-reader users may encounter a link without being told what it does or where it goes.

Location

Affected HTML

</a>

axe automated evidence 

Fix all of the following:
  Element is in tab order and does not have accessible text

Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have text that is visible to screen readers
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute

Custom scanner evidence

Link has no accessible name. Add meaningful link text, aria-label, or image alt text.

axe description

Ensure links have discernible text

Recommended change

Provide meaningful visible link text or another valid accessible name. Icon-only links should expose a concise accessible name describing their action or destination.

Context-Aware Link Recommendation

Destination / action: /star-multimedia/news/why-cant-the-worsening-law-and-order-situation-be-curbed-4259996

No automatic link name proposed

The available destination and contextual evidence was not strong enough to generate a specific accessible name safely.

Recommended action: Inspect the link's actual destination or action and provide a concise accessible name describing that purpose. Do not invent a name from weak visual or filename evidence.

Why this suggestion was made: No reliable destination, functional icon, accessible-name source, or specific contextual evidence was available.

Issue: missing accessible name Decision: insufficient evidence Context confidence: low Evidence: insufficient evidence

Human verification: Required before implementation.

This candidate was generated by deterministic destination and context rules. Confidence describes the strength of the available evidence and does not establish WCAG conformance.

Suggested code pattern 

<a aria-label="Describe link destination" href="/star-multimedia/news/why-cant-the-worsening-law-and-order-situation-be-curbed-4259996" hreflang="en"><img alt="" class="image-style-small-80x80" height="80" loading="lazy" src="/sites/default/files/styles/small_80x80/public/2026-08/law%20order.jpg?h=c673cd1c" width="80"/>
</a>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Verify the final computed accessible name in the rendered browser accessibility tree.

#101

Link does not have a discernible accessible name

link-name  •  UF-00101
High axe Links WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value Level A Axe automated finding Link recommendation V4
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Screen-reader users may encounter a link without being told what it does or where it goes.

Location

DOM selector: .mt-2\.5 | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<a href="#" class="headar-icon search-icon justify-between mt-2.5">

axe automated evidence 

Fix all of the following:
  Element is in tab order and does not have accessible text

Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have text that is visible to screen readers
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute

axe description

Ensure links have discernible text

Recommended change

Provide meaningful visible link text or another valid accessible name. Icon-only links should expose a concise accessible name describing their action or destination.

Context-Aware Link Recommendation

Destination / action: #

Suggested accessible name:
“Search”

Recommended action: Expose the search control with the accessible name 'Search'. If activating it performs an interface action rather than navigation, also review whether a <button> is the more appropriate semantic element.

Why this suggestion was made: The destination/function can be derived from explicit link or icon evidence without guessing visual meaning.

Issue: missing accessible name Decision: icon function search Context confidence: high Evidence: explicit search icon in link HTML

Evidence used: #

Element semantics also require review

This element may perform an interface action rather than navigation. Verify whether a semantic <button> would be more appropriate than a link.

Human verification: Required before implementation.

This candidate was generated by deterministic destination and context rules. Confidence describes the strength of the available evidence and does not establish WCAG conformance.

Link V4 Suggested HTML 

<a aria-label="Search" class="headar-icon search-icon justify-between mt-2.5" href="#"></a>

Manual review

Required: Yes

Verify the final computed accessible name in the rendered browser accessibility tree.

Reference

Methodology note: Automated accessibility testing can identify many important problems, but it cannot establish complete WCAG conformance. Context-dependent and incomplete findings require human review. Context-aware recommendations are produced by deterministic rules using extracted local page context and should be verified before implementation. VLM-assisted image recommendations use visual-semantic evidence from a local vision-language model, followed by deterministic accessibility guardrails. They remain human-review recommendations rather than automatic WCAG conformance decisions.
